about.heading: About
about.bio: I'm a final-year B.Tech CSE (Data Science) student at NIIT University, building end-to-end AI and ML systems rather than notebooks — an agentic RAG pipeline that audits insurance bills clause-by-clause with zero fabricated citations, a Kubernetes autoscaler that forecasts traffic and beats the stock autoscaler by 62% (and honestly reports where it didn't), a support platform that classifies every incoming complaint and routes it by urgency, a customer analytics pipeline that turns raw transactions into ranked retention decisions, and a hybrid recommender built to replace a feature that turned out to be a hardcoded constant. I care most about systems that measure their own claims instead of asserting them.

projects.name: Bill Auditor
projects.description: Insurers deduct from a hospital bill without saying which clause allowed it. This reads the bill against the policy line by line and names the clause behind every rupee removed.
bullets: Zero fabricated clause citations across all recorded evaluation versions
Hybrid dense + lexical retrieval (ChromaDB + BM25) with cross-encoder reranking over a 399-clause index
LLM never performs arithmetic — all money math runs in Python, keeping every figure verifiable
492 unit tests across an 8-stage Jenkins pipeline, deployed to Kubernetes

projects.name: Predictive Autoscaling for Kubernetes

metric.caption: Three runs per arm, identical traffic

projects.description: Kubernetes adds pods only after CPU has already climbed, so every traffic ramp is served short while new pods boot. This forecasts the load and scales before it arrives.
bullets: Cut p99 latency 62% (479 → 183 ms) against the stock autoscaler — three runs per arm, identical traffic, for 28% more compute
Quantile forecast on 39 time-series features, tuned to over-predict since running short costs 10x more
On a spike it cannot anticipate, forecasting alone was 40% worse — raising the autoscaler's floor instead came in 49% better
Safety checks declined to act on 23% of 980 logged decisions where the forecast wasn't trustworthy

projects.name: Complaint Triage System

metric.caption: 78.8% exact, 0.79 macro-F1 on a held-out set

projects.description: Support teams read every complaint before they know which one is urgent. This scores each one the moment it arrives, so the queue is sorted by urgency instead of arrival time.
bullets: Classifier reaches 78.8% accuracy and 0.79 macro-F1 on a held-out test set, and defers low-confidence cases to a human
DistilBERT sentiment feeds a transparent rules engine that sets priority — Low, Medium, High or Urgent
Gemini drafts the reply, grounded in the complaint's own text; an agent edits it before anything is sent
Three services, 227 tests across four suites, containerised and deployed to Kubernetes by a Jenkins pipeline

projects.name: Customer Segmentation & Retention
projects.description: Retention budget gets spread evenly across customers, including the ones who were never going to leave. This ranks who is actually worth keeping, and who isn't.
bullets: Processes 540K+ raw transactions into 391K validated records across 4,334 customers
Crosses BG/NBD + Gamma-Gamma lifetime value with XGBoost churn risk (0.78 ROC-AUC) into an action matrix
Flagged 229 high-value, high-risk customers worth £16.5K in predicted 90-day revenue
MLflow experiment tracking and DVC data versioning, served via FastAPI and a React dashboard

projects.name: MSME Marketplace

metric.caption: From zero coverage to three suites

projects.description: An inherited marketplace shipped a recommendation feature that was a hardcoded constant. I audited the code and built the real one.
bullets: Hybrid recommender as its own FastAPI service — content similarity blended with co-purchase filtering
Rebuilt auth on httpOnly cookies with refresh-token rotation, and fixed the access-control bugs the audit found
From zero tests to 133; three services on AWS k3s with automatic TLS
